title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Public Security on Issuing the Summary of the Joint Conference on Handling Criminal Cases of Illegal Operation of International Telecommunications Services
keywords_en: Criminal case of operating international telecommunications business
full_text_en:
Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Public Security on Issuing the Summary of the Joint Meeting on Handling Cases of Illegal International Telecom Business Crimes

Gongtong Zi [2002] No. 29

To the High People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, and Public Security Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Courts and Military Procuratorates of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; and the People's Procuratorate and Public Security Bureau of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

On November 20, 2002, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Information Industry convened a joint meeting in Beijing to study and resolve issues concerning the application of law in the current special campaign against crimes of illegal international telecom business. The Summary of the Joint Meeting on Handling Cases of Illegal International Telecom Business Crimes, as formed at the meeting, is hereby issued to you for compliance and implementation.

April 22, 2003

Summary of the Joint Meeting on Handling Cases of Illegal International Telecom Business Crimes

Illegal international telecom business not only disrupts the management order of the international telecom market, causes huge losses to national telecom tariffs, but also seriously endangers national information security.

On May 12, 2000, the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Disrupting the Management Order of the Telecom Market (hereinafter referred to as the "Interpretation"), on April 18, 2001, the Supreme People's Procuratorate and the Ministry of Public Security's Provisions on Standards for Prosecution of Economic Crime Cases, and on February 6, 2002, the Supreme People's Procuratorate's Reply on the Application of Law to Acts of Illegal International Telecom Business or Telecom Business with Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan were successively issued and implemented, playing an important role in enabling public security and judicial organs to accurately and promptly crack down on such crimes using legal weapons. Starting from September 17, 2002, public security organs at all levels have carried out a nationwide special campaign against illegal international telecom business. Due to the complexity, high specialization, strong technical nature, and constantly evolving criminal methods of illegal international telecom business activities, new situations and problems have emerged, such as telecom operators colluding with other enterprises or individuals to jointly carry out illegal business activities; perpetrators using new technical means to commit crimes. To accurately and uniformly apply the law, ensure the in-depth development of the special campaign, and investigate and punish criminal activities of illegal international telecom business according to law, on November 20, 2002, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Information Industry convened a joint meeting in Beijing to jointly study the issues concerning the application of law in the work of cracking down on crimes of illegal international telecom business, reaching a consensus on some issues. The summary of the meeting is as follows:

1. Public security organs, people's procuratorates, and people's courts at all levels, when handling cases of illegal international telecom business crimes, shall recognize the significant importance of cracking down on such criminal activities from the perspective of safeguarding national information security, maintaining the management order of the telecom market, and protecting national telecom revenue. They shall actively participate in the special campaign, perform their respective duties, cooperate with each other, strengthen coordination, and speed up the progress of case handling.

2. Article 1 of the Interpretation stipulates: "Whoever, in violation of state regulations, by leasing international dedicated lines, privately setting up switching equipment, or using other methods, engages without authorization in international telecom business or telecom business involving Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan for profit-making activities, thereby disrupting the management order of the telecom market, if the circumstances are serious, shall be convicted and punished for the crime of illegal business operation in accordance with the provisions of Item (4) of Article 225 of the Criminal Law." Operating without obtaining a license for international telecom business (including telecom business involving Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan; the same below), or continuing to operate after the qualification for international telecom business has been terminated, shall be deemed as "engaging without authorization in international telecom business or telecom business involving Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan"; if the circumstances are serious, criminal liability for the crime of illegal business operation shall be pursued in accordance with the above provisions.

The term "other methods" as used in Article 1 of the Interpretation refers to methods such as privately setting up cross-border communication lines in border areas; using the Internet to transmit IP voice across borders and setting up switching equipment to transfer international calls to the domestic public telephone network or to other countries or regions; setting up switching platforms within the country by means of leasing, hosting, or maintenance outsourcing; and privately setting up international communication gateways.

3. Operators who have obtained licenses for international telecom business (including operators of telecom business involving Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan), knowing that others are illegally engaging in international telecom business, nevertheless violate state regulations by means such as leasing, cooperation, or authorization, providing operational and technical conditions to others, utilizing existing equipment or setting up additional international call switching equipment for profit, if the circumstances are serious, shall be pursued for criminal liability as accomplices to the crime of illegal business operation.

4. When public security organs investigate cases of illegal international telecom business crimes, they shall promptly and comprehensively collect and secure criminal evidence, and swiftly apprehend criminal suspects. For cases of illegal international telecom business crimes currently being handled by people's procuratorates and people's courts, as long as the basic facts of the crime are clear and the basic evidence is reliable and sufficient, they shall promptly file a prosecution and render a judgment according to law. If the principal offender is at large, but the basic evidence for the crimes committed by other suspects or defendants in the case is reliable and sufficient, they may be dealt with first according to law.

5. Adhere to the criminal policy of "combining punishment with leniency." For principal offenders in joint crimes of illegal international telecom business and for state functionaries who collude with criminals, punishments shall be imposed strictly according to law. For those who voluntarily surrender, perform meritorious service, or have other statutory circumstances for lenient or mitigated punishment, they shall be given a lenient or mitigated punishment according to law.

6. Any problems encountered in handling cases of illegal international telecom business crimes in various localities, as well as information on investigations, prosecutions, and trials, shall be promptly reported to the respective higher competent authorities. Higher authorities shall strengthen supervision, inspection, guidance, and coordination of cases.

April 22, 2003
